# Vibe Acceptance Auditor

Review code and evidence independently. The implementation conversation is not an input. Never edit production, tests, configuration, dependencies, AppSpec or delivery state. Check commands may update build caches and write logs/receipts. The launcher writes audit/launch artifacts.

Read the immutable request first. For `mode: lean`, follow [lean-audit.md](references/lean-audit.md). For a Protocol 2.0 strict request, follow [strict-audit.md](references/strict-audit.md). Missing formal intermediate handoffs are not gaps in lean delivery. Bounded maintenance does not automatically require this full audit.

Build the normative inventory from AppSpec prose, flows, screens, ACs, managed operations and gates before trusting implementer claims. Trace real entry point  state/actions  domain/data/platform  observable result  meaningful assertions and completed checks. Inspect failure, restart, cancellation and lifecycle branches. Flag demo/fake production paths, unused assets, disconnected settings and tests that bypass actual wiring.

Use every required verification surface. Reuse current executed checks after examining their assertions and logs. Run missing or suspect checks. Distinguish unsupported host execution from a repository-verifiable failure; compilation never substitutes for iOS simulator/runtime evidence.

For Android, verify the shared [Android minimum SDK contract](../vibe-developer/references/android-platform-contract.md): `minSdk >= 24` in effective configuration and applicable built manifests. Report lower values as gaps; release readiness also needs the release AAB check when distribution is in scope.

For UI review actual primary-screen goldens and distinct rendering risks, localization/accessibility, assets and production use. Group repeated design patterns instead of requiring per-control paperwork. User/AppSpec requirements take precedence over default matrix size.

Return PASS only when all available requirements are independently substantiated and no local gap remains; otherwise GAPS or BLOCKED with exact obligation, failed link and smallest useful proof. External limitations prevent full completion as appropriate. A prior PASS is stale after changed inputs until revalidated. An auditor must never implement its own findings.

# Lean independent acceptance

The lean request fixes AppSpec/workspace fingerprints and unavailable host pairs. Read normative AppSpec sources before work.json or implementer summaries. Inventory approved/excluded requirements, ACs, managed operations and gates using the shared canonical helpers. Inspect normative omissions in prose too. Record reviewed Markdown paths once; no heading-by-heading justification for contextual prose.

Inspect every required `(obligation, surface)` pair from `verification_surface_map(app)` in `vibe_protocol.py`. For each verified pair record real production and test anchors, the assertion that proves behavior, and executed check receipts. Inspect receipt tasks and logs; a zero exit code alone, an unrelated assertion, skipped tests or an unconnected preview is insufficient. Check shared fixtures against actual production graph and platform wiring.

Run missing safe checks using `lean-delivery.py <repo> check`. Use `--runner gradle` for Gradle to hold the workspace mutex. Current global receipts may be reused without running the same matrix again. Do not change source/tests to make an audit pass. description: Independently check full KMP delivery against its approved AppSpec and actual production behavior; report gaps without implementing fixes.

# Vibe Acceptance Auditor

Review code and evidence independently. The implementation conversation is not an input. Never edit production, tests, configuration, dependencies, AppSpec or delivery state. Check commands may update build caches and write logs/receipts. The launcher writes audit/launch artifacts.

Read the immutable request first. For `mode: lean`, follow [lean-audit.md](references/lean-audit.md). For a Protocol 2.0 strict request, follow [strict-audit.md](references/strict-audit.md). Missing formal intermediate handoffs are not gaps in lean delivery. Bounded maintenance does not automatically require this full audit.

Build the normative inventory from AppSpec prose, flows, screens, ACs, managed operations and gates before trusting implementer claims. Trace real entry point → state/actions → domain/data/platform → observable result → meaningful assertions and completed checks. Inspect failure, restart, cancellation and lifecycle branches. Flag demo/fake production paths, unused assets, disconnected settings and tests that bypass actual wiring.

Use every required verification surface. Reuse current executed checks after examining their assertions and logs. Run missing or suspect checks. Distinguish unsupported host execution from a repository-verifiable failure; compilation never substitutes for iOS simulator/runtime evidence.

For Android, verify the shared [Android minimum SDK contract](../vibe-developer/references/android-platform-contract.md): `minSdk >= 24` in effective configuration and applicable built manifests. Report lower values as gaps; release readiness also needs the release AAB check when distribution is in scope.

For UI review actual primary-screen goldens and distinct rendering risks, localization/accessibility, assets and production use. Group repeated design patterns instead of requiring per-control paperwork. User/AppSpec requirements take precedence over default matrix size.

Return PASS only when all available requirements are independently substantiated and no local gap remains; otherwise GAPS or BLOCKED with exact obligation, failed link and smallest useful proof. External limitations prevent full completion as appropriate. A prior PASS is stale after changed inputs until revalidated. An auditor must never implement its own findings.

# Lean independent acceptance

The lean request fixes AppSpec/workspace fingerprints and unavailable host pairs. Read normative AppSpec sources before work.json or implementer summaries. Inventory approved/excluded requirements, ACs, managed operations and gates using the shared canonical helpers. Inspect normative omissions in prose too. Record reviewed Markdown paths once; no heading-by-heading justification for contextual prose.

Inspect every required `(obligation, surface)` pair from `verification_surface_map(app)` in `vibe_protocol.py`. For each verified pair record real production and test anchors, the assertion that proves behavior, and executed check receipts. Inspect receipt tasks and logs; a zero exit code alone, an unrelated assertion, skipped tests or an unconnected preview is insufficient. Check shared fixtures against actual production graph and platform wiring.

Run missing safe checks using `lean-delivery.py <repo> check`. Use `--runner gradle` for Gradle to hold the workspace mutex. Current global receipts may be reused without running the same matrix again. Do not change source/tests to make an audit pass. The launcher persists your final JSON; never create launch evidence yourself.

Return JSON with:

```json
{
  "requestSha256": "actual request file sha256",
  "startedAt": "actual RFC3339 time",
  "completedAt": "actual RFC3339 time",
  "inventory": {"requirementIds": [], "excludedRequirementIds": [], "acceptanceScenarioIds": [], "managedOperationIds": [], "qualityGateIds": []},

  ],
  "findings": [],
  "verdict": "PASS"
}
```

Use actual inventory, paths, symbols, times and receipts. Include all pairs, not only the illustration. `result` is `verified`, `gap`, `unavailable` or `not-applicable`. Gaps need reason and actionable findings. Unavailable is only for exact host pairs in the request; inspect the implementation that can be checked locally. Not-applicable is only for inactive conditional external/release gates and must name the condition and why it is inactive. No implicit waivers of repository behavior.

For the independent audit surface of the closure gate, use `result: verified`, `auditEvidence: true` and an assertion explaining the inventory/wiring review; the launcher/validator supplies its own execution proof instead of requiring a recursively pre-existing audit receipt. This exception applies only to a surface named `independent-audit` or `acceptance-audit` or `audit` on a gate, never to product tests.

PASS means all locally available obligations are proven, no local gap or finding remains. GAPS lists known missing behavior/evidence; BLOCKED explains why a reliable assessment is unavailable. For delta review, inspect changed file hashes and consumers, close previous findings with new proof and return a complete current inventory. Request a fresh full audit if scope or independence no longer permits delta review.

# Product

## Product promise

**SproutPace** helps a home grower with several trays know what each tray needs next and plan repeated harvests within the places actually available.

- Store name EN: **SproutPace: Microgreens**
- Store name RU: **SproutPace: Микрозелень**
- Promise EN: **Know what each tray needs next.**
- Promise RU: **Понятный следующий шаг для каждого лотка.**

The name describes a growing rhythm; it must never imply that the app accelerates biological growth. Brand, domain, trademark, and store-name availability must be rechecked before publication.

## Problem and audience

The primary user is a home grower who manages a small set of concurrent trays and may still be completing a first cycle. The user may grow on a windowsill, under a lamp, or use both. They need to coordinate soaking, sowing, blackout/weight, light growth, moisture checks, harvest, and the next sow without maintaining a spreadsheet or accepting an impossible capacity plan.

The product is intended for adults managing home growing. It is not directed to children. Android is the first publication target in all store-supported countries; the interface is EN/RU with English fallback. iOS is fully implemented and verified in the current scope but not published.

## Core outcome

The primary planning goal is a user-selected harvest frequency across a rotation of cultures. A secondary continuous-queue mode suggests the next batch so another tray approaches harvest after the preceding one. Neither mode models household consumption or guarantees continuous food availability.

The first-value loop is:

1. Define at least one light growing zone and a tray size.
2. Choose harvest cadence and cultures.
3. Accept a feasible proposed batch.
4. Confirm real stage changes and see recalculated future actions.
5. Complete or close the batch.
6. Start or accept the next cycle without an external calendar or spreadsheet.

## MVP scope

- Four stable destinations: Today, Trays, Plan, and Catalog.
- Optional first-run setup; catalog browsing remains available before setup.
- Named light and dark zones with integer place capacity. One growing batch occupies one practical place; geometry packing is out of scope.
- Rectangular and circular metric tray-size presets.
- Eight built-in cultures: radish, broccoli, arugula, mustard, pea, sunflower, basil, and garden cress (`Lepidium sativum`, not watercress).
- Versioned offline catalog with source metadata, EN/RU resource keys, ranges, food-safety guidance, and metric seed-density calculations.
- Personal recipes, supplier/variety/seed-lot notes, substrate choice, optional germination percentage, and immutable per-batch recipe snapshots.
- Batch stages: optional soaking, sown, blackout/weight when applicable, light growth, ready for harvest, and terminal harvested/failed/abandoned outcomes.
- Manual confirmation, correction, last-transition undo, explicit stage skip, capacity conflict resolution, and temporary unassigned placement.
- Today actions, one conditional daily summary, and a separate best-effort target-time soak reminder without Android exact-alarm permission.
- Cadence plan, future capacity validation, explicit confirmation before creating suggested batches, and continuous-queue suggestions.
- Dated observations with optional local photo.
- History, optional actual harvest mass, repeat-as-new-batch, explicit permanent deletion, and no trash.
- Local full backup/replace restore with photos and relationships; photo-free CSV history export.
- Local data reset.
- Two approved Android inline Yandex ad placements with fail-closed privacy gating; iOS production ads disabled because no iOS ad project/ID exists in scope.
- Firebase Crashlytics on Android and iOS release builds, default on with Settings opt-out, no Firebase Analytics.
- Light/dark/system theme, EN/RU, accessibility, adaptive widths, and offline-first core.

## Non-goals

The excluded requirements REQ-901 through REQ-909 are normative. In particular, the MVP has no account, cloud sync, app backend, AI/OCR diagnosis, IoT, social network, commerce, farm inventory, subscription, paid tray limit, video lessons, consumption/storage tracking, predicted yield, monthly calendar, Analytics, attribution, fullscreen/rewarded/app-open ads, iOS publication, or iOS production ads.

## Product principles

- Record reality before protecting the plan: an actual stage change may be saved even when configured capacity is full.
- Never shift a user-confirmed date silently.
- A forecast is a range or suggestion, not a biological guarantee.
- No streaks, artificial daily check-ins, or growth-speed promises.
- Core actions never wait for network, advertising, or Crashlytics.
- Ads never cover primary content or appear in a critical grow action.
- User-authored names, notes, recipes, and photographs remain user data.

## Success criteria

The MVP succeeds when a home grower can configure places, follow one batch to a recorded outcome, and create or accept a second cycle without an external spreadsheet. The leading product signal is progression to the second cycle, not a daily streak. Because product analytics are excluded, validate this through pilot task testing and interviews rather than hidden event collection.

## Assumptions and limitations

- Exact culture ranges vary by seed lot, cultivar, tray, medium, light, temperature, and user technique.
- Seed mass is a metric recommendation derived from growing area and versioned density guidance, always editable for a batch.
- Physical validation of several real cycles is not yet complete and must not be claimed.
- Built-in catalog maintenance is intentionally lightweight: change a simple catalog version and review date, update source metadata, and pass QG-011. No external approval, signature, or attestation workflow exists.
- Final privacy-policy URL/copy, Firebase files, Android Yandex ad ID, signing, store accounts, and publication state are external inputs tracked by quality gates.

## Evidence used during product definition

# Domain

## Glossary

- **Grow zone**: a named physical area with a type and integer place capacity. Types are natural light, grow light, and dark.
- **Place**: the user's practical unit for one tray; SproutPace does not solve geometric packing.
- **Tray-size preset**: rectangular width/length or circular diameter in centimetres.
- **Built-in culture**: versioned app-owned catalog entry with stable ID and localized resource keys.
- **User grow recipe**: user-authored stages and guidance, clearly separated from built-in content.
- **Recipe snapshot**: immutable copy of the parameters used to create a batch.
- **Grow batch**: one planned or actual cultivation cycle.
- **Stage event**: a user-confirmed actual transition with timestamp and optional skip/correction context.
- **Scheduled action**: a derived next action for a batch; it is not a habit streak.
- **Harvest plan**: cadence, selected culture rotation, mode, and future suggestions.
- **Observation**: dated private text with an optional app-owned local photo.
- **Outcome**: harvested, failed, or abandoned terminal state.
- **Continuous queue**: a planner mode that suggests a next batch; it does not track consumption or stored harvest.

## Stable built-in identities

The first catalog version contains these language-neutral IDs:

| Stable ID | EN key | RU key meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `radish` | `culture_radish_name` | редис |
| `broccoli` | `culture_broccoli_name` | брокколи |
| `arugula` | `culture_arugula_name` | руккола |
| `mustard` | `culture_mustard_name` | горчица |
| `pea` | `culture_pea_name` | горох |
| `sunflower` | `culture_sunflower_name` | подсолнечник |
| `basil` | `culture_basil_name` | базилик |
| `garden_cress` | `culture_garden_cress_name` | кресс-салат |

`garden_cress` means `Lepidium sativum`; do not label it Watercress or model `Nasturtium officinale` as the same culture.

## Grow-zone invariants

- Capacity is a non-negative integer.
- At least one light-capable place is required before the planner can call a plan feasible.
- A dark zone is optional. Covered or stacked germination on a light shelf continues to occupy that light place.
- Soaking occupies no grow place.
- A sown or growing batch occupies at most one configured place, or is explicitly `unassigned` with a visible warning.
- Moving between zones releases the prior place and claims the new place as one transaction.
- An actual stage event is never rejected solely because configured capacity is full; use another place, change capacity, or record `unassigned`.
- Historical batches preserve zone-name snapshots when a zone is renamed or deleted.

## Tray and seed recommendation invariants

- Rectangular area is width × length; circular area is π × diameter² ÷ 4.
- All persisted dimensions use metric units.
- Recommended seed mass is derived from area and the recipe's versioned density input, then displayed in grams.
- The recommendation is editable per batch and never represented as a guarantee.
- Supplier, cultivar, seed-lot text, and germination percentage are optional user data.

## Recipe invariants

- Built-in recipes are read-only, versioned, source-attributed, and resolved through resource keys.
- A built-in recipe may be duplicated into a user recipe.
- Personal recipes support create/read/update/delete/duplicate.
- Changing or deleting a recipe never mutates a batch's recipe snapshot.
- Built-in instructions use ranges for soaking, blackout/weight, transition-to-light, and harvest window when supported by sources.
- Food-safety guidance covers untreated/microgreen-intended seed, food-safe clean containers, drinking water, drainage, avoiding excessive moisture, and allergy awareness.
- Photographs and illustrations are not diagnostic references.

## Batch state machine

Planned batches may proceed through only applicable states:

`planned → soaking? → sown → blackout_or_weight? → light_growth → ready_for_harvest → harvested`

From any non-terminal state the user may close as `failed` or `abandoned`. A recipe may omit soaking or blackout/weight. A user may explicitly skip a configured stage; the event remains recorded.

Terminal outcomes are historical records, not deletion. Permanent deletion is a separate confirmed operation. Repeating creates a new planned batch with a new ID and snapshot; it never reopens or mutates the original.

## Scheduling rules

- Recommended dates are projections until the user confirms the real event.
- Confirming an early or late stage recalculates only dependent future actions from the actual transition.
- An explicitly user-fixed harvest date is never changed silently; conflicts are shown.
- Undo reverses only the most recent transition, restores the preceding state, and cancels/rebuilds affected future reminders idempotently.
- Short soak duration uses elapsed-time semantics. Calendar actions use local civil date/time and follow a changed time zone.
- Notification identifiers are stable by action ID so restart, restore, undo, and rescheduling cannot create duplicates.
- Android exact-alarm special access is not requested. Delivery near a soak target is best-effort and the authoritative due state remains visible in-app.

## Planner rules

- A harvest plan has a cadence, selected rotation, mode (`cadence` or `continuous_queue`), and paused state.
- Suggestions use recipe ranges and known place capacity; they are never batches until confirmed.
- A plan with unresolved overlap is labeled `needs_resolution`; the UI offers another date, another zone, or capacity change.
- Confirmed dates are not shifted silently.
- Editing, pausing, or deleting a plan changes future suggestions only. Confirmed and active batches persist.
- Continuous queue means another batch is approaching harvest; it does not guarantee edible stock at home.

## Observation and outcome rules

- Observations are ordered by actual timestamp and preserve user text verbatim.
- Photo files are private app-owned data selected through the system picker and linked by stable observation ID.
- Deleting an observation removes its linked file. Deleting a batch removes all linked observation files.
- Harvest outcome accepts optional actual mass, note, and result assessment. There is no predicted mass.
- Harvested, failed, and abandoned outcomes all release capacity and cancel future reminders.

## Error semantics

- Managers return Kotlin `Result` and preserve the original failure cause.
- Persistence/file failures do not partially report success.
- Restore validates into a staging boundary before replacement; any invalid archive leaves current data untouched.
- Capacity conflicts are domain results with resolution choices, not generic exceptions.
- Network, privacy endpoint, advertising, and Crashlytics failures never fail a core product operation.
- Coroutine cancellation is never swallowed by broad error capture.


# Data

## Local persistence

Use a shared Kotlin Multiplatform database for relational product data, typed Multiplatform Settings for small preferences/privacy caches, and private app storage for imported observation photos. Managers own persistence boundaries; Stores never call database or platform APIs directly.

Expected local records include:

- grow zones and capacity;
- tray-size presets;
- personal recipes and recipe stages;
- grow batches with immutable recipe, tray, substrate, culture, supplier/cultivar/lot, and zone-name snapshots;
- stage events and derived scheduled actions;
- harvest plans and suggestions;
- observations and photo references;
- terminal outcomes and optional actual mass;
- notification preferences and stable scheduled IDs;
- theme preference;
- Crashlytics collection preference;
- one versioned advertising privacy payload containing only the minimal endpoint response, current choice, and matching policy version.

Use stable language-neutral IDs and foreign keys. Do not persist resolved built-in translations.

## Managed operations

`app-spec.json#managedEntities` is authoritative. Important consequences:

- Deleting zones, presets, or recipes does not erase immutable batch snapshots.
- Delete and terminal batch outcomes are different operations.
- Backup archives are immutable external files; create another archive rather than updating one.
- Ad-consent withdrawal is an update, not deletion.
- Crash reporting always has a default-on release preference and is disabled by updating that preference.

## Built-in catalog

Ship catalog content as versioned, deterministic local seed/reference data with stable culture IDs and string-resource keys. Recommended structure:

- `catalogVersion`: a simple monotonic content version;
- `reviewedOn`: content update date;
- culture ID and scientific/common-name resource keys;
- source URL/title metadata;
- stage applicability and duration ranges;
- blackout/weight and presoak flags/ranges;
- metric density input and its source/version;
- substrate/lighting notes as resource keys;
- safety note keys;
- illustration resource name.

Updating the catalog needs no external approval, signature, or attestation. It must change the version/date, preserve IDs where semantics are unchanged, document sources, and pass QG-011. A breaking identity change requires an explicit migration.

## Localized text storage

The complete English key set lives in `shared/compose/src/commonMain/composeResources/values/strings.xml`; Russian lives in `values-ru/strings.xml`. Catalog seed data and database rows contain only IDs/resource keys. Resolve keys to generated `Res.string.*` accessors at the presentation boundary.

User-authored recipe names, supplier/lot notes, observations, and batch notes are stored verbatim and are not resource strings. Native-only Android/iOS permission and platform text uses native localized resources with English base and Russian addition.

## Backup archive

The full backup is a versioned local archive selected through the platform document provider. It contains:

- a manifest with schema/version and counts;
- all product records and stable relationships;
- app-owned observation photos with integrity metadata;
- user preferences needed to restore product behavior;
- no Crashlytics server data, advertising SDK cache, detected country/IP, advertising ID, or secrets.

Before restore, parse and validate the complete archive, show a localized preview, and require explicit replacement confirmation. Replacement is transactional: stage files and database content, commit both, then rebuild only future reminders. Invalid or unsupported archives leave existing data and files untouched. Restoring the same archive again replaces rather than merges, so it cannot duplicate records.

CSV export contains a localized or documented stable header contract for batch history, culture/recipe identity, relevant dates, outcome, actual mass, and user notes as appropriate. It excludes photographs and does not serve as a restorable backup.

## Remote APIs

### Privacy-region endpoint

Use `GET https://168.222.252.178/v1/privacy/region` exactly as defined by the monetization contract. Send no query parameters or user/install/location identifiers. Accept only strict schema 1 JSON with exact JSON content type, a supported policy version string, and `expiresAt` no more than 72 hours ahead. Reject redirects, non-200 responses, malformed/oversized/non-UTF-8 bodies, unknown schema, stale/overlong expiry, and transport failures.

The endpoint is an accepted shared service. Do not create a backend, alternative service, live qualification, readiness attestation, or endpoint-specific release gate.

### Yandex Ads

Send only the configured ad-unit ID unless a later approved privacy inventory adds something. No product data, notes, schedules, culture choices, photos, user ID, location, or account data enters an ad request. Debug/test uses test IDs; previews and automated tests make no real requests.

### Firebase Crashlytics

Crashlytics is configured separately for Android and iOS release/release-candidate builds. Do not add Firebase Analytics. Do not set a user ID or log user-authored text, crop/recipe selections, schedules, photos, advertising state, or breadcrumbs. Allowed context is limited to app version, platform/build, stack traces, ANR/fatal data, selected technical non-fatals, and reviewed non-PII technical keys.

The release default is collection enabled. The persisted user toggle disables or re-enables future collection according to the platform SDK contract. Local reset does not claim to delete reports already sent to Firebase.

## Offline and cache behavior

- Core database, catalog, photos, plan, history, backup, export, and Settings work offline.
- A valid privacy-region response may be cached only until its accepted expiry, clamped to 72 hours.
- Missing/stale privacy data disables ads for that launch; it does not delay app startup or core screens.
- Crash reports may remain queued by the native SDK contract, but upload never blocks the UI.
- There is no cloud sync, merge policy, login token, or remote product cache.

## Retention and erasure

Product data remains until the user deletes individual records, uses Delete all local data, clears app storage, or uninstalls. Delete all removes database rows, private photos, product/settings state, ad-consent payload, and scheduled reminders, then returns to first run. It explains that previously sent Crashlytics reports and externally saved backup/CSV files are not deleted.


# Quality

## Non-functional requirements

- Core local operations remain usable without network and do not wait for ads, privacy lookup, or Crashlytics.
- Database and file mutations are transactional where partial success could break relationships.
- Today and batch detail open from local state without visible network delay.
- Image import, hashing, backup, restore, and CSV export do not block the main thread and expose cancellation/failure cleanly.
- Notification scheduling, restart, undo, restore, and time-zone changes are idempotent.
- Sensitive/user-authored content is absent from logs, ad requests, and Crashlytics.

Reject custom generic Success/Failure wrappers, nested `Result<Result<T>>`, lost nullable successes, swallowed cancellation, duplicate mutable state ownership, component-to-database calls, raw Store state exposed as UI model, stateful Compose previews, dependency cycles, and incorrect lifecycle/resource ownership.

## Delivery and verification boundaries

The approved process transition is recorded in `../docs/decisions/DEC-20260920-lean-delivery.md`. Lean delivery is current: one owner per complete scenario, direct checks with execution logs, compact `.vibe/work.json`/recovery notes, early production-root integration, risk-based golden review and independent final audit. Future visual variants cover primary screens in light/dark and distinct risk states; choose additional stress combinations by risk/pairwise coverage without reducing explicit screen contracts. Architecture flexibility governs future work and does not require rewriting existing tested modules/Stores. Existing lint and coverage thresholds remain binding; any actual policy change needs a scoped decision, never a workaround for a failed test.

Batch detail uses a vertical stage timeline with actual events, predicted windows, skipped markers, and the next action. Stage illustrations are decorative support and never diagnostic evidence.

Capacity is shown as named zones and occupied/available counts. Future conflicts use warning roles plus explicit text and actions: choose another date, choose/add a zone, change capacity, or retain `needs_resolution`. Actual overflow uses the same language but includes `Temporarily unassigned` so a user can record reality.

Allowed slots only:

- SCREEN-007: one clearly labeled inline ad after the fourth culture card.
- SCREEN-003 History tab: one clearly labeled inline ad after the fifth historical record.

At most one ad is visible per eligible screen visit. No app-forced refresh loop is required. Ads are absent from short lists, empty/loading/error states, first run, Today, active batch detail, editors, stage confirmation, completion, planning decisions, settings, permissions, backup, and privacy.

No fill, offline, missing/stale eligibility, declined/unresolved consent, missing ID, SDK error, or iOS no-ID collapses the slot without blocking or leaving a misleading placeholder.

- Default theme policy is system. Settings options are System, Light, and Dark.

- Use Material spacing tokens based on the 8dp system and minimum 48×48dp targets.
- Prefer tonal surface hierarchy over heavy shadows; keep elevation levels few.

- All bundled copy, errors, accessibility labels, catalog text, and preview text resolves from production EN/RU resources with shared keys.
- User names and notes wrap as data; do not attempt to localize them.
- Titles may use two lines at compact widths before truncation. Critical culture/batch names remain visible; secondary metadata may ellipsize only after its most useful prefix.

- Meaningful headings and logical reading/focus order.
- Screen-reader action/state names for every control and dynamic status announcement for completed/rescheduled/conflict actions.

- Local content never shows a false network-offline error.
- Catalog is bundled and available offline.
- Ads disappear when network/privacy is unavailable.

/** File-backed test host port: external exports survive private import cleanup. */
internal class PublicFileDocuments(private val directory: Path) : ArchiveDocumentPort {
    private fun path(id: String): Path {
        require(id.matches(Regex("[A-Za-z0-9._-]+")))
        return directory.resolve(if (id.startsWith("imported")) "imports" else "exports").resolve(id)
    }
    override suspend fun read(documentId: String): ByteArray? = path(documentId).takeIf(Files::exists)?.let(Files::readAllBytes)
    override suspend fun write(documentId: String, bytes: ByteArray) {
        val file = path(documentId)
        Files.createDirectories(file.parent)
        Files.write(file, bytes)
    }
    override suspend fun clearImportedArchives() {
        val imports = directory.resolve("imports")
        if (Files.exists(imports)) Files.list(imports).use { entries -> entries.forEach(Files::delete) }
    }
}

internal suspend fun withPublicWorkspace(block: suspend (Path, MapSettings) -> Unit) {
    val directory = Files.createTempDirectory("sproutpace-public-")
    try { block(directory, MapSettings()) } finally {
        Files.walk(directory).use { entries -> entries.sorted(Comparator.reverseOrder()).forEach(Files::delete) }
    }
}

# Quality

## Non-functional requirements

- Core local operations remain usable without network and do not wait for ads, privacy lookup, or Crashlytics.
- Database and file mutations are transactional where partial success could break relationships.
- Today and batch detail open from local state without visible network delay.
- Image import, hashing, backup, restore, and CSV export do not block the main thread and expose cancellation/failure cleanly.
- Notification scheduling, restart, undo, restore, and time-zone changes are idempotent.
- Sensitive/user-authored content is absent from logs, ad requests, and Crashlytics.

## Test matrix

Use deterministic clocks, IDs, file systems, notification schedulers, region responses, ad hosts, Crashlytics facades, and catalog fixtures.

Required repository coverage:

- domain tests for tray area, seed mass, stage applicability, early/late transitions, skip/undo, elapsed soak duration, local civil scheduling, cadence/continuous suggestions, and capacity conflicts;
- manager/persistence tests for every managed CRUD operation, snapshot immutability, terminal outcomes, referential integrity, photo cleanup, restart, and failure cause preservation;
- MVIKotlin Store tests for intent/action/message/reducer behavior, cancellation, retries, exactly-once completion, and no production mutation outside Stores;
- Decompose component tests for public component models, navigation outputs, tabs, editors, destructive confirmation, permission recovery, and expanded list-detail behavior;
- notification tests for summary grouping, no-work silence, soak target, permission denial, restart/restore idempotence, cancellation, and time-zone change;
- backup/archive tests in QG-012;
- privacy/network/ad lifecycle tests in QG-009 consumer scope only;
- Crashlytics facade/config tests proving release default-on, opt-out persistence, build-type disabling, and no Analytics/user identifiers;
- EN/RU resource completeness, stable catalog key mapping, system locale changes, unsupported-locale EN fallback, native fallback resources, and hardcoded-string scan;
- Detekt with no auto-regenerated baseline;
- filtered Kover baseline measured on owned product code before selecting a fixed threshold;
- applicable Gradle compilation/test tasks through the repository wrapper.

QG-001 owns this matrix. Warnings are reported separately from failures.

## Android platform gate

QG-002 requires:

- release/test build and process-restart smoke;
- notification permission denied/granted flows and system-settings recovery;
- best-effort soak target without `USE_EXACT_ALARM` or `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` declarations;
- system photo picker and document create/open flows;
- Yandex automatic initialization disabled until the privacy gate permits it;
- Android Yandex manifest/SDK linkage, debug test IDs, release ID guard, no overlap/inset defects, and no request in ineligible states;
- Crashlytics Android configuration, mapping upload path, opt-out behavior, and controlled test crash for release candidate;
- Compose resources, EN/RU/native strings, system theme/insets, and platform accessibility smoke.

## iOS platform gate

QG-003 requires evidence from macOS and CI for both declared iOS targets:

- framework/app compilation and native entry point;
- notification authorization/denial, scheduling, cancellation, restart, and time-zone behavior;
- photo and document pickers plus private file persistence;
- Firebase Crashlytics Apple configuration, dSYM upload/symbolication path, opt-out behavior, and controlled test crash;
- Yandex integration remains safe-disabled without an iOS production ad unit; no production ad request occurs;
- Compose/native EN/RU resources, system theme/safe areas, VoiceOver, and expanded/compact behavior.

Absence of a Mac receipt is an unresolved required platform gate, not evidence of success.

## Visual quality gate

QG-007 requires:

- component-owned preview implementations, not local Compose-only fakes;
- nonzero ComposablePreviewScanner discovery;
- early production render smoke containing real theme/font/resources in light/dark and RU at 200%;
- applicable content/empty/error/offline/permission/conflict/destructive states for all primary screens;
- compact and expanded layouts;
- Paparazzi record, human inspection, approval, and verify with stable IDs;
- accessibility inspection for reading order, labels, state announcements, focus, contrast, non-color cues, 48dp targets, reduced motion, clipping, and EN/RU glyphs;
- first-release Lazyweb review of the full primary-screen golden set and disposition of every blocking finding.

## Catalog quality

QG-011 verifies:

- exactly the approved eight stable culture IDs, including `garden_cress` as `Lepidium sativum` and no watercress alias;
- catalog version and review date;
- reachable source metadata and concise original paraphrases rather than copied instructions;
- stage ranges, applicability, density units/formulas, metric display, and editable recommendation behavior;
- food-safety copy and non-diagnostic image/copy boundaries;
- complete EN/RU resource keys and offline resolution;
- simple internal versioning only—no external approval, signature, attestation, or invented physical-test receipt.

## Backup quality

QG-012 uses fixtures covering every managed entity, historical snapshots, stage events, schedules, observations, UTF-8 EN/RU/user text, and multiple photo files.

Verify create → preview → replace restore → restart equality; future-only reminder rebuild; overdue in-app actions; no completed reminders; repeat restore without duplicates; invalid/malformed/unsupported archive rollback; cancellation; insufficient storage/write failure; missing/corrupt photo rejection; and CSV escaping/encoding without photos.

## Advertising and privacy verification

Use the canonical endpoint and test only the consuming app. Controlled responses cover fresh cache, expired cache, protected, non-protected, unknown, malformed/oversized/non-JSON/non-UTF-8, redirect, 429, 503, timeout, TLS/captive/offline, unknown schema, overlong expiry, policy change, accept, decline, withdrawal, and restart.

- at most one refresh path and a maximum 72-hour accepted cache;
- app-owned consent appears only when required;
- no Yandex SDK initialization or load before eligibility;
- `YandexAds.setUserConsent(...)` precedes every allowed initialization;
- decline/unresolved/stale/error/no-ID states produce no init, request, or visible slot;
- withdrawal stops future requests without affecting product data;
- only SCREEN-007 after item four and SCREEN-003 History after item five are eligible;
- previews/tests use safe-disabled hosts and no real requests;
- no endpoint smoke, readiness attestation, backend gate, alternative endpoint, CMP/TCF claim, mediation, Google demand, advertising ID, ATT, or location inference is added.

## Crashlytics verification

- Release default is enabled; user can disable/re-enable from Settings and the choice survives restart.
- Preview, debug, unit, screenshot, and automated test hosts do not upload.
- Firebase Analytics is absent and breadcrumb collection is not enabled.
- No user ID, notes, photos, culture/recipe, schedule, advertising state, or private data is logged as keys/messages.
- Only reviewed technical non-fatals are recorded.
- Android mapping and iOS dSYM symbolication are proven on controlled release-candidate crashes when QG-008 applies.
- Privacy disclosures explain default collection, opt-out, and that local reset cannot erase reports already sent.

## Accessibility and localization

Require base EN and complete RU Compose Multiplatform resources with identical keys; OS-only locale selection; no language picker, locale preference, or app-specific override. Unsupported locales fall back to EN. Native-only text follows the same default/additional locale contract.

All screens support 200% text, screen readers, keyboard/pointer input where exposed, visible focus, reduced motion, 48dp targets, logical heading/order, manual date/time input, and non-color cues. Production previews use production resources and fonts.

## Architecture checks

Reject custom generic Success/Failure wrappers, nested `Result<Result<T>>`, lost nullable successes, swallowed cancellation, duplicate mutable state ownership, component-to-database calls, raw Store state exposed as UI model, stateful Compose previews, dependency cycles, and incorrect lifecycle/resource ownership.

Require Decompose public components, MVIKotlin Stores for independent mutable/async state (read-only children may project parent state), injectable service or Manager boundaries returning Kotlin `Result`, pure reducers, immutable component models, manual DI/factories, and separate preview components. The screenshot host remains the Compose UI/resource-owning module unless a documented build limitation requires the approved dedicated-host alternative.

## Asset delivery

QG-006 follows the asset contract. Every ASSET item must have a delivered runtime file, manifest hash, provenance/rights, reachable production usage, and applicable visual evidence. Generated culture covers need generation records and source/rights notes. Standard Material vectors use standard-icon evidence only when unchanged and correctly identified. All resources compile on Android and iOS and render at declared sizes in production previews.

Platform launcher/store icon derivatives are verified with platform-specific mask/background/export rules even though the shared logo source is in Compose Resources.

## External configuration

- QG-005: Android store publication, signing, store listing, countries, current name check, and publication result only when publishing.
- QG-008: separate Firebase Android/iOS app registrations, configuration files, symbol upload, and controlled readable crash reports for release candidates.
- QG-009: Android Yandex project/ad unit and device verification when production ads are enabled. No iOS production ad project is required in scope.
- QG-010: final privacy-policy URL/copy and store/platform disclosures when externally distributing.

Do not invent credentials, IDs, URLs, console state, publication success, or external receipts. Do not create a release gate for the accepted shared privacy endpoint.

## Release acceptance

QG-004 requires:

- strict AppSpec validation and canonical inventory parity;
- all active ACs verified on their declared surfaces;
- QG-001, QG-002, QG-003, QG-006, QG-007, QG-011, and QG-012 current and successful;
- each conditional external gate either proven when its condition is active or clearly reported as inactive/blocked-external;
- build/test CI for Android and iOS; publishing automation only when publication scope is explicitly activated;
- pinned tested dependency/SDK versions; separate upgrades use authoritative release/migration sources and verify artifact availability;
- one frozen integration matrix and independent acceptance audit with current fingerprints;
- separate reporting of locally verified, implementation complete, and release ready.

Validator success alone does not prove product content, platform behavior, external configuration, physical grow validation, implementation completion, or release readiness.

## Delivery and verification boundaries

The approved process transition is recorded in `../docs/decisions/DEC-20260920-lean-delivery.md`. Lean delivery is current: one owner per complete scenario, direct checks with execution logs, compact `.vibe/work.json`/recovery notes, early production-root integration, risk-based golden review and independent final audit. Strict ledger/assignment/handoff history is preserved but not extended. Do not import historical verified claims as current proof.

Use affected tests during iteration and one complete applicable matrix at a stable snapshot. After bounded fixes the same independent auditor reviews changed code and dependent behavior; changes to AppSpec or broad architecture start a fresh audit. Known gaps are auditable and prevent false completion. Preserve all approved acceptance surfaces, existing tests and goldens. Future visual variants cover primary screens in light/dark and distinct risk states; choose additional stress combinations by risk/pairwise coverage without reducing explicit screen contracts. Record shared M3 choices once and inspect every affected screen locally; reuse or group external review by screen family.

Architecture flexibility governs future work and does not require rewriting existing tested modules/Stores. Existing lint and coverage thresholds remain binding; any actual policy change needs a scoped decision, never a workaround for a failed test.

# SCREEN-009 — Observation editor

Linked flows: FLOW-007  
Linked requirements: REQ-007

## Purpose and hierarchy

Add or edit a dated observation with optional note and one optional app-owned photo selected through the system picker.

## States

- Create/edit content with date, note, and photo preview.
- Photo absent, selected, replaced, or removed.
- Picker permission/failure explanation that preserves text.
- Validation and local save failure with retry.
- Offline: fully available.

## Actions and iconography

Save is primary; Choose/Replace photo, Remove photo, Delete observation, and Cancel are labeled. Use standard photo, date, save, delete, and navigation icons; photo thumbnails never become unlabeled controls.

## Text layout expectations

User notes preserve entered language and line breaks. Date follows system locale. At 200% supporting/error text wraps below its field; destructive labels remain complete.

## Responsive, accessibility, and insets

Compact uses a scrolling form; expanded gives the photo a bounded supporting pane. Picker use is not the only path to save. Preview has a useful description derived from localized context, not image diagnosis. Scaffold owns insets once.

## Allowed ad slots

None.

## Asset requirements

Standard photo, date, save, delete, and back icons.

## Preview and golden matrix

Empty create light/dark; note plus photo; edit; RU 200%; long note; picker failure; delete confirmation; local save error; expanded photo pane.

# SCREEN-010 — Close batch

Linked flows: FLOW-008  
Linked requirements: REQ-008

## Purpose and hierarchy

Record an explicit terminal outcome—harvested, failed, or abandoned—with date and optional outcome-specific details before freeing capacity.

## States

- Harvested: optional actual mass and note.
- Failed: optional reason and note.
- Abandoned: optional reason and note.
- Validation: invalid date or mass remains inline.
- Local save failure retains all fields; offline is fully available.

## Actions and iconography

Save outcome is primary; Cancel leaves the batch active. Outcome uses radio buttons or a connected group, never icon-only selection. Standard harvest, failed, abandoned, date, mass, and save icons supplement labels.

## Text layout expectations

Outcome consequences are plain complete sentences. Mass uses an explicit metric unit and accepts no implied forecast. At 200% choices and actions stack without clipping.

## Responsive, accessibility, and insets

Compact may use a full-height form instead of a cramped dialog; expanded may use a basic modal with bounded width. Focus starts at the heading/outcome, validation is announced, and cancellation has predictable back behavior.

## Allowed ad slots

None.

## Asset requirements

Standard harvest, failed, abandoned, date, mass, save, and close icons.

## Preview and golden matrix

# FLOW-004 — Create and advance a grow batch

Linked requirements: REQ-004  
Linked screens: SCREEN-002, SCREEN-003, SCREEN-004, SCREEN-005, SCREEN-006, SCREEN-012

## Goal

Create one batch from a recipe snapshot and keep its real state, capacity, and future actions correct through edits and stage transitions.

## Entry and exit conditions

Enter from New batch, a plan suggestion, recipe Use action, or existing batch detail. Exit after a persisted edit/transition/deletion or return with no change.

## Ordered steps

1. Select recipe, tray, substrate, optional seed metadata, start/date intent, and place when applicable.
2. Save a planned batch snapshot.
3. Confirm real soaking/sowing/stage events.
4. Recalculate dependent future actions and capacity atomically.
5. Correct, undo, skip, or permanently delete only through explicit actions.

## Branches and resume

Actual reality may be saved as temporarily unassigned. Persistence failure leaves the prior state. Fixed user dates become visible conflicts instead of silently moving.

## AC-030

Given a valid recipe and tray choice exist on SCREEN-004
When the user saves a new planned batch
Then GrowBatch is created with a new ID and immutable recipe/tray/substrate snapshot and appears on SCREEN-003.

## AC-031

Given GrowBatch was persisted
When the application restarts and SCREEN-003 or SCREEN-005 opens
Then its planned/actual stages, snapshot, placement, actions, and terminal state are restored.

## AC-032

Given an existing GrowBatch is opened from SCREEN-005 into SCREEN-004
When the user corrects culture metadata, tray, place, seed amount, or actual dates and confirms the shown consequences
Then only dependent future actions are recalculated and past events remain explicit.

## AC-033

Given a GrowBatch is still planned on SCREEN-003 or SCREEN-004
When the user confirms permanent deletion
Then that batch is removed without creating history or a trash record.

## AC-034

Given a GrowBatch is active or terminal on SCREEN-005
When the user passes the stronger permanent-delete confirmation
Then its records, observations, and app-owned photo files are removed and no future reminder remains.

## AC-035

Given the recipe includes soaking and a planned batch exists
When the user starts soaking from SCREEN-005
Then an actual soaking event and elapsed target are stored while no GrowZone place becomes occupied on SCREEN-002.

## AC-036

Given a planned/soaking batch and a compatible configured place exist
When the user confirms sowing on SCREEN-005
Then the batch enters its first growing stage and exactly one place on SCREEN-012 becomes occupied.

## AC-037

Given an active GrowBatch has a predicted next stage
When the user confirms the actual transition on SCREEN-005
Then the actual timestamp is recorded, old placement is released/new placement claimed when needed, and only dependent future dates update on SCREEN-002 and SCREEN-006.

## AC-038

Given the user physically moves a batch but every configured destination place is occupied
When they confirm the actual move on SCREEN-005
Then SCREEN-012 offers choose/add/change-place options and permits a visible temporarily unassigned state instead of rejecting reality.

## AC-039

Given an active batch has at least one reversible latest stage event
When the user chooses Undo last transition on SCREEN-005
Then only that transition is reversed and affected placements/actions/reminders are rebuilt once.

## AC-040

Given an applicable configured stage has not occurred
When the user confirms Skip stage on SCREEN-005
Then the skip is recorded explicitly and future actions are derived from the next applicable state.
